# Usage patterns

Usage patterns are small, reusable examples for things that come up again and again when a
catalysis dataset is described: a synthesis with its precursors, a measurement with a
specific technique, a catalytic test in a fixed bed, a simulation and its results. Each
pattern states its purpose, shows a real use case and the fields involved, and gives the
example three ways: as a graph, as YAML (the format you write) and as RDF/Turtle (what a
knowledge graph receives).

Every example is an excerpt of one of the [community datasets](community-datasets.md) or of the
[spreadsheet example](building-a-parser.md#jlcat03). It is validated against the current schema
whenever the documentation is built, so it can be copied as a starting point. For *why* the schema is structured this way, see
[Design Patterns](../design-patterns.md); for every field, see the
[Schema Reference](../elements/overview.md).

**Legend of the graphs:**

<span style="background:#cfe9ef;border:1px solid #00838f;border-radius:4px;padding:1px 6px;margin:2px;display:inline-block;color:#222">Dataset</span> <span style="background:#fde2c4;border:1px solid #c26b00;border-radius:4px;padding:1px 6px;margin:2px;display:inline-block;color:#222">Activity (synthesis, characterization, simulation, reaction)</span> <span style="background:#e3dcf7;border:1px solid #5b3fb5;border-radius:4px;padding:1px 6px;margin:2px;display:inline-block;color:#222">Plan (method, technique, protocol)</span> <span style="background:#d4ecd6;border:1px solid #2e7d32;border-radius:4px;padding:1px 6px;margin:2px;display:inline-block;color:#222">Entity (sample, catalyst, precursor, chemical)</span> <span style="background:#d5e6f7;border:1px solid #1565c0;border-radius:4px;padding:1px 6px;margin:2px;display:inline-block;color:#222">Agent (instrument, reactor)</span> <span style="background:#fff4c2;border:1px solid #9a7d00;border-radius:4px;padding:1px 6px;margin:2px;display:inline-block;color:#222">Quantity (value or range with unit)</span> <span style="background:#f3e5f5;border:1px solid #8e24aa;border-radius:4px;padding:1px 6px;margin:2px;display:inline-block;color:#222">Qualitative value or calculated property</span> <span style="background:#fce4ec;border:1px solid #ad1457;border-radius:4px;padding:1px 6px;margin:2px;display:inline-block;color:#222">Vocabulary term</span> <span style="background:#eeeeee;border:1px solid #757575;border-radius:4px;padding:1px 6px;margin:2px;display:inline-block;color:#222">Literal value</span>

Boxes show an object's title (or id) and, in «guillemets», its class. Arrows are labelled with the field that links two objects. Descriptions are left out of the graph; the YAML tab shows the full excerpt.

## Section 1: Describing a dataset

Everything starts with a `CatalysisDataset`: it says what the data is, who made it, which
catalysis field it belongs to, and which activities produced it.

### Pattern 1 – A dataset, its classification and its activities { #dataset-entry-point }

**Purpose:** Make a dataset findable and classifiable: a persistent identifier, a title, the catalysis research field as a vocabulary term, the people behind it, the publication that uses it, and where the files are.

**Example use case:** A deposit of thermocatalytic NH₃ decomposition data. The research field is *heterogeneous catalysis* (`voc4cat:0007001`); the dataset was produced by, among other activities, a temperature-programmed reduction, described under `was_generated_by_characterization`.

**Notes:**

- Each activity is described under the field for its kind: `was_generated_by_synthesis`, `was_generated_by_characterization` or `was_generated_by_simulation`. The field tells software which kind it is, and in RDF the activity gets the matching class (here OBI:0000070, assay).
- `was_generated_by` lists the ids of all activities; DCAT-AP-PLUS requires it on every dataset. In RDF both fields become the same `prov:wasGeneratedBy` links.
- `is_referenced_by` links the dataset to the article; the article usually cites the dataset only by its handle, so this is the way back.

**Fields used:** [`rdf_type`](../elements/slots/rdf_type.md), [`keyword`](../elements/slots/keyword.md), [`creator`](../elements/slots/creator.md), [`name`](../elements/slots/name.md), [`publisher`](../elements/slots/publisher.md), [`is_referenced_by`](../elements/slots/is_referenced_by.md), [`dataset_distribution`](../elements/slots/dataset_distribution.md), [`access_URL`](../elements/slots/access_URL.md), [`licence`](../elements/slots/licence.md), [`was_generated_by`](../elements/slots/was_generated_by.md), [`was_generated_by_characterization`](../elements/slots/was_generated_by_characterization.md), [`carried_out_by`](../elements/slots/carried_out_by.md), [`evaluated_entity`](../elements/slots/evaluated_entity.md), [`realized_plan`](../elements/slots/realized_plan.md), [`plan_designator`](../elements/slots/plan_designator.md)

## Section 2: Catalyst synthesis

A `Synthesis` takes precursors (`had_input_entity`), follows a preparation method
(`realized_plan`) and produces catalyst samples (`had_output_entity`). The method's class
decides which parameters it can carry.

### Pattern 2 – A synthesis with precursors, amounts and a typed preparation method { #synthesis-coprecipitation }

**Purpose:** Record what went into a catalyst, how much of it, and the conditions of the preparation method as structured values.

**Example use case:** Co-precipitation of a Cu–Al–Ga hydrotalcite precursor from three metal nitrates at pH 9, aged at 65 °C and calcined. The plan declares itself a `CoPrecipitation` (`plan_designator: voc4cat:0007795`), which makes the precipitation, ageing and calcination fields available.

**Notes:**

- `plan_designator` takes the `class_uri` of the method exactly as written in the schema (`voc4cat:…` in lower case). Without it, the method fields still validate as JSON but cannot be loaded into the Python datamodel.
- Some quantity fields take a list even when there is one value (e.g. `has_ph_value`), others a single value (e.g. `has_aging_duration`). The schema reference shows which.

**Fields used:** [`nominal_composition`](../elements/slots/nominal_composition.md), [`catalyst_measured_properties`](../elements/slots/catalyst_measured_properties.md), [`had_input_entity`](../elements/slots/had_input_entity.md), [`precursor_quantity`](../elements/slots/precursor_quantity.md), [`had_output_entity`](../elements/slots/had_output_entity.md), [`realized_plan`](../elements/slots/realized_plan.md), [`plan_designator`](../elements/slots/plan_designator.md), [`precipitating_agent`](../elements/slots/precipitating_agent.md), [`has_ph_value`](../elements/slots/has_ph_value.md), [`has_aging_temperature`](../elements/slots/has_aging_temperature.md), [`has_aging_duration`](../elements/slots/has_aging_duration.md), [`has_calcination_temperature_range`](../elements/slots/has_calcination_temperature_range.md), [`has_calcination_atmosphere`](../elements/slots/has_calcination_atmosphere.md)

### Pattern 3 – A preparation in two steps { #synthesis-multi-step }

**Purpose:** Describe a preparation that uses two different methods one after the other, without losing which method and which conditions belong to which step.

**Example use case:** A Cu–Al oxide is co-precipitated and calcined (step 1); then 1 wt% Ga is added by incipient wetness impregnation and the material is calcined again (step 2). The intermediate oxides are the output of step 1 and the input of step 2, which chains the two `Synthesis` records.

**Notes:**

- The chain is made by using the same `id` for the intermediate in both records. Each step can then declare its own method class.
- Precursor masses are recommended, not mandatory. Articles often give only target loadings, as here.

**Fields used:** [`rdf_type`](../elements/slots/rdf_type.md), [`was_generated_by`](../elements/slots/was_generated_by.md), [`was_generated_by_synthesis`](../elements/slots/was_generated_by_synthesis.md), [`nominal_composition`](../elements/slots/nominal_composition.md), [`catalyst_measured_properties`](../elements/slots/catalyst_measured_properties.md), [`had_input_entity`](../elements/slots/had_input_entity.md), [`had_output_entity`](../elements/slots/had_output_entity.md), [`realized_plan`](../elements/slots/realized_plan.md), [`plan_designator`](../elements/slots/plan_designator.md), [`has_calcination_temperature_range`](../elements/slots/has_calcination_temperature_range.md), [`impregnation_type`](../elements/slots/impregnation_type.md)

## Section 3: Characterization

A `Characterization` is carried out by an instrument (`carried_out_by`), evaluates samples
(`evaluated_entity`) and follows a technique (`realized_plan`). The technique's class decides
which parameters it can carry.

### Pattern 4 – A measurement with a typed technique and its parameters { #characterization-typed-technique }

**Purpose:** Say which technique was used, on which sample, with which instrument, and record the technique-specific parameters in their own fields.

**Example use case:** H₂ temperature-programmed reduction of a Ni-BCZY cermet: 10% H₂ in Ar, 10 K/min up to 1223 K, TCD detection. The plan is declared as `TPR` (`plan_designator: CHMO:0002908`), the same term that classifies the activity (`rdf_type`).

**Notes:**

- `rdf_type` on the activity classifies the measurement for search; `plan_designator` on the plan selects the technique class and its fields. Both point to the same CHMO term here.

**Fields used:** [`rdf_type`](../elements/slots/rdf_type.md), [`carried_out_by`](../elements/slots/carried_out_by.md), [`evaluated_entity`](../elements/slots/evaluated_entity.md), [`realized_plan`](../elements/slots/realized_plan.md), [`plan_designator`](../elements/slots/plan_designator.md), [`has_temperature_range`](../elements/slots/has_temperature_range.md), [`has_heating_rate`](../elements/slots/has_heating_rate.md), [`reducing_gas_composition`](../elements/slots/reducing_gas_composition.md)

### Pattern 5 – One technique, many samples { #characterization-many-samples }

**Purpose:** Keep records short when one technique is applied to a whole sample series: one `Characterization` per technique, listing every sample it was applied to.

**Example use case:** BET surface area of ten Pd/P catalysts on Al₂O₃ and SiO₂ (three shown here). The technique is classified by an ENM term; the instrument model was not stated in the source and is described as such.

## Section 4: Catalytic testing

A `CatalyticReaction` names the reaction, its catalysts, reactants and products, the reactor
it ran in and the conditions. Group runs that share reactor and analytics into one record.

### Pattern 6 – Catalysts, reactants and products { #reaction-participants }

**Purpose:** Identify what reacted over which catalyst: chemicals as ChEBI terms, catalysts with the elements they are composed of and their nominal loadings.

**Example use case:** Ammonia decomposition over Ru/Ba catalysts on a Ni-BCZY cermet (two of six catalysts shown). Ammonia and argon are reactants, nitrogen and hydrogen products. Each catalyst lists ruthenium and barium under `composed_of`, each with its loading as a mass fraction in percent.

**Notes:**

- A loading belongs to a component, not to the catalyst as a whole: list the components under `composed_of`, each with its ChEBI term, and give each its own mass fraction. Properties of the whole catalyst, such as its BET surface area or mass, stay on the catalyst.
- Each component gets its own `id` (here the catalyst's id plus the element symbol), because its loading applies only within this catalyst. The chemical identity is shared through `rdf_type`.

**Fields used:** [`reaction_name`](../elements/slots/reaction_name.md), [`rdf_type`](../elements/slots/rdf_type.md), [`catalyst_type`](../elements/slots/catalyst_type.md), [`catalyst_form`](../elements/slots/catalyst_form.md), [`used_catalyst`](../elements/slots/used_catalyst.md), [`composed_of`](../elements/slots/composed_of.md), [`has_quantitative_attribute`](../elements/slots/has_quantitative_attribute.md), [`used_reactant`](../elements/slots/used_reactant.md), [`generated_product`](../elements/slots/generated_product.md), [`used_reactor`](../elements/slots/used_reactor.md), [`reactor_designator`](../elements/slots/reactor_designator.md)

### Pattern 7 – Reactor, conditions and product analysis { #reaction-reactor-conditions }

**Purpose:** Describe where and under which conditions a catalytic test ran, and how the products were measured.

**Example use case:** A quartz packed bed (0.8 cm inner diameter, 1.2 cm bed, catalyst diluted with silica) at 1 bar, ramped from 473 to 873 K with 500–3000 ppm NH₃ in Ar; the effluent was analysed by online FTIR. The reactor is declared a `FixedBedReactor` (`reactor_designator: coremeta4cat:FixedBedReactor`).

**Notes:**

- Declaring the reactor type restricts its fields: fixed-bed fields on a reactor declared as an autoclave fail validation.
- Space velocity and results such as conversion or T₁₀/T₅₀ have no field yet; they go into `description` for now.

**Fields used:** [`rdf_type`](../elements/slots/rdf_type.md), [`catalyst_mass`](../elements/slots/catalyst_mass.md), [`used_reactor`](../elements/slots/used_reactor.md), [`reactor_designator`](../elements/slots/reactor_designator.md), [`catalyst_bed_diameter`](../elements/slots/catalyst_bed_diameter.md), [`catalyst_bed_height`](../elements/slots/catalyst_bed_height.md), [`catalyst_dilution_material`](../elements/slots/catalyst_dilution_material.md), [`product_identification_method`](../elements/slots/product_identification_method.md), [`reactor_temperature_range`](../elements/slots/reactor_temperature_range.md), [`experiment_pressure`](../elements/slots/experiment_pressure.md), [`feed_composition_range`](../elements/slots/feed_composition_range.md)

## Section 5: Simulation

A `Simulation` names its software, the method it realized (`realized_plan`), what it
modelled (`evaluated_entity`) and the properties it computed (`calculated_property`).

### Pattern 8 – A simulation with a typed method and calculated properties { #simulation-dft-properties }

**Purpose:** Record which code and method produced a set of computed values, and what they were computed for.

**Example use case:** DFT binding energies of OH and CO at doped CuGa₂O₄ sites (VASP, PBE). The plan is declared as `DFT` (`plan_designator: coremeta4cat:DFT`) so the functional has its own field, and each binding energy as `AdsorptionEnergetics` (`property_designator: coremeta4cat:AdsorptionEnergetics`) so the adsorbate and the energy reference have their own fields.

**Notes:**

- `property_designator` works like `plan_designator`: it names the property class an entry belongs to (adsorption, reaction or transition-state energetics, electrochemical free energy, catalytic descriptors, or one of the material properties). Without it, an entry can only carry a value and a description.
- The deposit gives the binding energies as ranges over 17 sites, so the range stays in `value`; a single computed energy goes into `adsorption_energy` as a number in eV.

**Fields used:** [`software_package`](../elements/slots/software_package.md), [`rdf_type`](../elements/slots/rdf_type.md), [`evaluated_entity`](../elements/slots/evaluated_entity.md), [`realized_plan`](../elements/slots/realized_plan.md), [`plan_designator`](../elements/slots/plan_designator.md), [`exchange_correlation_functional`](../elements/slots/exchange_correlation_functional.md), [`calculated_property`](../elements/slots/calculated_property.md), [`property_designator`](../elements/slots/property_designator.md), [`adsorbate`](../elements/slots/adsorbate.md), [`material_composition`](../elements/slots/material_composition.md), [`energy_reference`](../elements/slots/energy_reference.md)

### Pattern 9 – Comparing variants with relative values { #simulation-relative-values }

**Purpose:** Report computed values that only make sense relative to a reference, and name the reference.

**Example use case:** MM/GBSA binding free energies of a PLP-bound substrate in two mutants of an amine transaminase, reported as ΔΔG relative to the parent enzyme 3FCR-4M.

**Fields used:** [`software_package`](../elements/slots/software_package.md), [`evaluated_entity`](../elements/slots/evaluated_entity.md), [`realized_plan`](../elements/slots/realized_plan.md), [`calculated_property`](../elements/slots/calculated_property.md)

### Pattern 10 – A simulation step that produces structures, not properties { #simulation-workflow-step }

**Purpose:** Describe workflow steps such as structure preparation, docking or molecular dynamics, whose result is a structure or trajectory file rather than a number.

**Example use case:** Desmond molecular dynamics of an enzyme–substrate complex in three variants. The plan is declared as `MolecularDynamics` (`plan_designator: NCIT:C18097`); there is no `calculated_property`.

**Notes:**

- `calculated_property` is recommended, not mandatory, for exactly this case.

**Fields used:** [`software_package`](../elements/slots/software_package.md), [`evaluated_entity`](../elements/slots/evaluated_entity.md), [`realized_plan`](../elements/slots/realized_plan.md), [`plan_designator`](../elements/slots/plan_designator.md)

## Section 6: Frequently applied patterns

Two things appear in almost every record: values with units, and terms from controlled
vocabularies.

### Pattern 11 – Values, ranges and fractions with units { #quantities }

**Purpose:** Write numbers so that software can compare them: a value or a range, the kind of quantity, and the unit, both as QUDT IRIs.

**Example use case:** A single pressure (1 bar), a temperature range (473.15–873.15 K) and a metal loading as mass fraction (0.5 wt% Ru), given on the ruthenium component of the catalyst.

**Notes:**

- Use full QUDT IRIs for `unit` (`https://qudt.org/vocab/unit/K`), not bare codes like `K`. Bare codes pass validation but cannot be resolved in RDF.
- `description` on a quantity is the place for context such as "nominal" or "constant across all runs".

**Fields used:** [`rdf_type`](../elements/slots/rdf_type.md), [`used_catalyst`](../elements/slots/used_catalyst.md), [`composed_of`](../elements/slots/composed_of.md), [`has_quantitative_attribute`](../elements/slots/has_quantitative_attribute.md), [`used_reactor`](../elements/slots/used_reactor.md), [`reactor_designator`](../elements/slots/reactor_designator.md), [`reactor_temperature_range`](../elements/slots/reactor_temperature_range.md), [`experiment_pressure`](../elements/slots/experiment_pressure.md)

### Pattern 12 – Classifying with vocabulary terms { #vocabulary-terms }

**Purpose:** Make records searchable across datasets by classifying them with terms from controlled vocabularies instead of free text.

**Example use case:** CO methanation classified by the Voc4Cat reaction term *hydrogenation* (`voc4cat:0000260`), with carbon monoxide identified by its ChEBI term.

**Notes:**

- `rdf_type` takes an object with the term's CURIE (`id`) and a readable label (`title`). Voc4Cat covers catalysis-specific terms; CHEBI, CHMO and NCIT are used for chemicals, techniques and general concepts.
- The reaction type is mandatory. Voc4Cat has no term for methanation yet, so the reaction uses the closest broader term, *hydrogenation*, and keeps the specific name in `reaction_name`.

**Fields used:** [`reaction_name`](../elements/slots/reaction_name.md), [`rdf_type`](../elements/slots/rdf_type.md), [`catalyst_type`](../elements/slots/catalyst_type.md), [`used_reactant`](../elements/slots/used_reactant.md), [`used_reactor`](../elements/slots/used_reactor.md)

### Pattern 13 – A preparation step the schema has no field for { #synthesis-step-without-field }

**Purpose:** Record a preparation step that the preparation method has no fields for, with its conditions as structured values, instead of squeezing it into the fields of another step.

**Example use case:** A Pt/Al₂O₃ catalyst is impregnated, dried and then reduced in 5 % H₂/N₂ up to 700 °C. `Impregnation` has drying and calcination fields but none for a reduction, so the reduction is a step of its own under `has_part`. It is typed with the Voc4Cat term *reduction* (`voc4cat:0000098`) and carries its conditions as typed attributes.

**Notes:**

- `has_part` takes any activity. Its conditions go into the generic `has_quantitative_attribute` and `has_qualitative_attribute`, each with a `title` and, where a vocabulary term exists, an `rdf_type`: here *atmosphere* (`voc4cat:0007809`), *heating rate* (`voc4cat:0008116`) and *gas flow rate* (`voc4cat:0008109`).
- Use the calcination fields only for a calcination. In the source workbook these columns were headed "calcination"; the data provider confirmed that the step was a reduction.

**Fields used:** [`nominal_composition`](../elements/slots/nominal_composition.md), [`catalyst_measured_properties`](../elements/slots/catalyst_measured_properties.md), [`had_input_entity`](../elements/slots/had_input_entity.md), [`realized_plan`](../elements/slots/realized_plan.md), [`plan_designator`](../elements/slots/plan_designator.md), [`impregnation_type`](../elements/slots/impregnation_type.md), [`has_drying_temperature`](../elements/slots/has_drying_temperature.md), [`has_drying_duration`](../elements/slots/has_drying_duration.md), [`has_part`](../elements/slots/has_part.md), [`rdf_type`](../elements/slots/rdf_type.md), [`has_qualitative_attribute`](../elements/slots/has_qualitative_attribute.md), [`carried_out_by`](../elements/slots/carried_out_by.md), [`has_quantitative_attribute`](../elements/slots/has_quantitative_attribute.md)

### Pattern 14 – A value the schema has no field for { #value-without-field }

**Purpose:** Keep a quantity that has no field of its own as a structured, typed value rather than as free text.

**Example use case:** The catalyst's metal loading, 5 wt% (nominal). CoreMeta4Cat has no metal-loading field, so the value is a generic quantity of the catalyst sample (`has_quantitative_attribute`), typed with the Voc4Cat term *metal loading* (`voc4cat:0008106`) and given as a mass fraction in percent.

**Notes:**

- `rdf_type` on the quantity says what it is; `has_quantity_type` and `unit` say how it is measured. Together they keep the value comparable across datasets.
- The same record uses the pattern for a qualitative value too: the reactor's operation mode (batch) is a `has_qualitative_attribute` typed *operation mode* (`voc4cat:0000108`).

**Fields used:** [`nominal_composition`](../elements/slots/nominal_composition.md), [`catalyst_measured_properties`](../elements/slots/catalyst_measured_properties.md), [`had_output_entity`](../elements/slots/had_output_entity.md), [`has_quantitative_attribute`](../elements/slots/has_quantitative_attribute.md), [`rdf_type`](../elements/slots/rdf_type.md), [`had_input_entity`](../elements/slots/had_input_entity.md), [`realized_plan`](../elements/slots/realized_plan.md), [`plan_designator`](../elements/slots/plan_designator.md)
